script.title: THE FACE-OFF
lines: HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank. India's two largest private banks.
Together they're worth over 24 lakh crore. But in the past year, ICICI Bank's share rose 16 percent, while HDFC Bank's fell 18.
So how do they really compare? Let's go through the numbers, one by one.

script.title: SIZE
lines: On size, HDFC Bank has a market cap of 12.6 lakh crore. ICICI Bank, 11.5 lakh crore.
HDFC Bank's yearly revenue is 3.08 lakh crore, about 1.8 times ICICI Bank, helped by its merger with HDFC Limited.

script.title: SHARE PRICE
lines: The two share prices have gone in opposite directions.
Over one year, ICICI Bank is up 16 percent. HDFC Bank, down 18.
Over three and five years: 16 to 20 percent a year for ICICI Bank, just 1 to 3 for HDFC Bank.
Over ten years: 21 percent a year, against 10.
Today, ICICI Bank is 1 percent below its 52-week high. HDFC Bank, 20 percent.

script.title: VALUATION
lines: Here's what you pay for each.
HDFC Bank trades at 16.4 times earnings. ICICI Bank, at 21.
On book value, HDFC Bank is at 2.2 times, ICICI Bank at 3.2.
And HDFC Bank's dividend yield is 1.6 percent, about double ICICI Bank's 0.75.

script.title: REVENUE GROWTH
lines: Since 2017, HDFC Bank's revenue grew from 69 thousand crore to 3.08 lakh crore, with a jump after its 2023 merger with HDFC Limited.
ICICI Bank grew from 54 thousand crore to 1.70 lakh crore.
That's about 18 percent a year for HDFC Bank, against 12 for ICICI Bank.

script.title: PROFIT GROWTH
lines: On profit, HDFC Bank earned 74.7 thousand crore last year. ICICI Bank, 50.1 thousand crore.
Ten-year profit growth: 20 percent a year at HDFC Bank, 18 at ICICI Bank. Over five years, ICICI Bank was faster, at 25.

script.title: LAST 8 QUARTERS
lines: Over the last eight quarters, both banks kept growing.
Quarterly revenue reached 83 thousand crore at HDFC Bank, and 49 thousand crore at ICICI Bank.
Quarterly profit grew 17 percent at HDFC Bank over two years, and 26 percent at ICICI Bank.

script.title: RETURN ON EQUITY
lines: For banks, the key efficiency measure is return on equity.
HDFC Bank held 16 to 18 percent for years, then slipped to 14 after the merger.
ICICI Bank climbed from 3 percent in 2019 to 16 today, now ahead of HDFC Bank.

script.title: BAD LOANS
lines: For any bank, the biggest risk is bad loans.
HDFC Bank's gross NPA fell from 1.24 to 1.11 percent of loans, with net NPA at 0.37.
ICICI Bank's fell faster, from 1.58 to 1.20 percent, with net NPA at 0.30.
ICICI Bank also earns a wider margin: 4.18 percent, against 3.32.

script.title: WHO OWNS IT
lines: Neither bank has a promoter. Institutions and the public own them.
At HDFC Bank, foreign investors cut their stake from 49 to 39 percent in two years, as domestic institutions rose to 43.
At ICICI Bank, foreign investors hold 35 percent, and domestic institutions 42.

script.title: LATEST QUARTER
lines: The latest quarter covers July to September 2026.
HDFC Bank's net interest income rose 9.7 percent, but profit just 4.7, as treasury gains fell.
ICICI Bank's net interest income rose 17.7 percent, profit 20 percent, and loans 30 percent.
But ICICI Bank's margin slipped to 4.18 percent, from 4.36.

script.title: STRENGTHS & WATCH-OUTS
lines: So, the strengths, and what to watch.
HDFC Bank: the biggest balance sheet, a lower valuation, and lower gross NPA. Watch: slow profit growth, and a lower return on equity.
ICICI Bank: faster profit growth, a higher return on equity, and a strong share price. Watch: a richer valuation, and a slipping margin.

script.title: THE SUMMARY
lines: HDFC Bank is the bigger bank, and the cheaper stock today.
ICICI Bank is growing faster, earns more on equity, and its share price shows it.
This is not a buy or sell call. Which one suits your style? Tell us in the comments.
